et leksikon.explanation: "Et leksikon" means "an encyclopedia". To look up the meaning of a word instead, use "en ordbog" (a dictionary): "Jeg slår ordet op i en ordbog" (I look the word up in a dictionary).

et lig.explanation: "Et lig" means "a corpse". It is a blunt word. A gentler way to speak of a dead person is "den afdøde" (the deceased person): "Familien sørger over den afdøde" (The family mourns the deceased person).

et like.explanation: "Et like" means "a like". To say you give one on social media, say: "Jeg giver et like" (I give a like).

et link.explanation: "Et link" means "a link". To ask someone to send one, say: "Send mig et link" (Send me a link).

et liv.explanation: "Et liv" means "a life". To talk about life in general, use the form "livet": "Livet er godt" (Life is good). To talk about one person's life, use "et liv": "at have et godt liv" (to have a good life).

et loft.explanation: "Et loft" means "a ceiling / attic". When you talk about the top of a room, it means "ceiling": "Der er en lampe i loftet" (There is a lamp in the ceiling). When you talk about the space under the roof, it means "attic": "Vi har gamle ting på loftet" (We have old things in the attic).

et loftsrum.explanation: "Et loftsrum" means "an attic room". It is built from "et loft" (an attic) and "et rum" (a room).

related.en: a top floor under the roof

et loppemarked.explanation: "Et loppemarked" means "a flea market". It is built from "en loppe" (a flea) and "et marked" (a market). To say you go to one, say: "Vi går på loppemarked i morgen" (We are going to a flea market tomorrow).

et lotteri.explanation: "Et lotteri" means "a lottery". To say someone won a prize in one, say: "Han vandt i lotteriet" (He won the lottery). The plural is "lotterier": "to lotterier" (two lotteries).

et lovforslag.explanation: "Et lovforslag" means "a bill". It is built from "lov" (law) and "et forslag" (a proposal). To say parliament approves one, use "at vedtage" (to pass): "Folketinget vedtager lovforslaget" (The Danish parliament passes the bill).

et lykønskningskort.explanation: "Et lykønskningskort" means "a congratulations card". It is built from "en lykønskning" (a congratulation) and "et kort" (a card). To congratulate someone aloud, say: "Tillykke!" (Congratulations!)

et lyskryds.explanation: "Et lyskryds" means "an intersection with traffic lights". It is built from "lys" (light) and "et kryds" (a cross). For an intersection without traffic lights, use "et vejkryds" (an intersection): "Vi mødes i vejkrydset" (We meet at the intersection).

et lån.explanation: "Et lån" means "a loan". The verb "at låne" means both "to borrow" and "to lend": "Jeg låner dig en pen" (I lend you a pen).

et lår.explanation: "Et lår" means "a thigh". To name a part of a chicken, put the animal in front: "et kyllingelår" (a chicken thigh).

et læserbrev.explanation: "Et læserbrev" means "a letter to the editor". It is built from "en læser" (a reader) and "et brev" (a letter). English speakers would guess the plural wrongly: it is "læserbreve", not "læserbrever".

et løbebånd.explanation: "Et løbebånd" means "a treadmill". It is built from "at løbe" (to run) and "et bånd" (a belt). The plural has no ending: "to løbebånd" (two treadmills).

et løfte.explanation: "Et løfte" means "a promise". To say you keep a promise, use "at holde" (to hold): "Jeg holder mit løfte" (I keep my promise). To say you break one, use "at bryde" (to break): "Han brød sit løfte" (He broke his promise).

et løg.explanation: "Et løg" means "an onion". The word is also part of "hvidløg" (garlic), literally "white onion".

lad os se.explanation: "Lad os se" means "Let's see." To suggest doing something together, put "lad os" (let us) before a verb: "Lad os gå" (Let us go). To say you will check, answer a question like this: "Er der mere mælk?" "Lad os se." (Is there more milk? Let's see.)

lad være.explanation: "Lad være" means "Don't!" To tell someone not to do something, add "med at" and a verb: "Lad være med at ringe" (Don't call). In the past, "lad" becomes "lod": "Han lod være" (He left it alone).

lakrids.explanation: "Lakrids" means "licorice". To name ice cream with that flavor, add "is" (ice cream): "lakridsis" (licorice ice cream).

laks.explanation: "Laks" means "salmon". To count whole fish, use "en laks" (a salmon): "Han fanger en laks" (He catches a salmon). To talk about salmon as food, leave out "en": "Jeg spiser laks" (I eat salmon).

laktosefri.explanation: "Laktosefri" means "lactose-free". It is built from "laktose" (lactose) and "fri" (free). The same ending is in "glutenfri" (gluten-free) and "sukkerfri" (sugar-free). With a word that takes "et", add "t": "et laktosefrit produkt" (a lactose-free product).

lammekød.explanation: "Lammekød" means "lamb", the meat. It is built from "et lam" (a lamb) and "kød" (meat).

lammet.explanation: "Lammet" means "paralyzed". To say someone is frozen by fear, use it too: "Hun stod lammet af skræk" (She stood paralyzed by fear). Do not mix it up with "lammet" meaning "the lamb", which is "et lam" (a lamb) with "the" added: "Lammet løber" (The lamb runs).
